company.name: Tunebox
company.description: Tunebox is a music streaming app that added podcasts two years ago.

title: Improve Tunebox for podcast listeners
brief: Podcasts are a quarter of new Tunebox sign-ups, but podcast listeners churn faster than music listeners and many move to a dedicated podcast app. You lead the podcast team. Read the research and answer like an interview: who exactly you improve it for, what problem, what you ship first and how you measure it.

segments.why: A minority of listeners but most of the listening hours, and the ones leaving for other apps. Keeping them is the podcast business.
Biggest by headcount, which makes them tempting, but most say they do not want podcasts. Volume is not need.
A clear need and a loud voice in reviews, but a niche next to commuters.
The question is about listeners. Creators matter, but they are a different product.

problems.why: Hits commuters every day at the exact moment they listen, and pushes them to apps that get it right.
Makes the daily habit harder to keep; second in the interviews.
Matters most to creators and music-first listeners. Commuters already know what they follow.
A real annoyance in tunnels and on planes, but less frequent than the two above.
The learners' top need; nice to have for everyone else.
A creator problem, outside a listener question.

solutions.why: Removes the commuters' biggest pain completely. The best value per unit of effort.
A cheap, good second step. It helps the habit but leaves the daily frustration in place.
Solves a smaller problem well. A sensible third item.
The tempting answer, aimed at music-first listeners who said they do not want podcasts. Large effort for the wrong problem.
Exactly right for language learners; little for commuters.

metrics.why: Measures the exact behavior you want to keep, for the segment you chose, and reads within weeks.
Related, but following is cheap; it does not show people stay.
The right guardrail: podcast changes on Home must not eat into music, which pays the bills.
Moves for many reasons and slowly; a business outcome, not a feature metric.
Mixes every segment; a shelf could lift it while commuters still leave.
Too slow and too noisy to judge one feature.

ideal.users: Daily commuters: about a fifth of podcast listeners but most of the hours, and the ones moving to other apps. Music-first listeners are the biggest group, but most of them told us they do not want podcasts.
ideal.problems: Losing their place between phone and car, then new episodes buried under music. Both break the daily habit that keeps commuters on Tunebox.
ideal.solutions: Ship resume on any device first: it removes the biggest pain for medium effort. Then the new episodes shelf, which is cheap, then smart downloads. AI recommendations are the tempting answer for the wrong segment.
ideal.metrics: Success: weekly podcast retention of commuters. Guardrail: music listening hours, so podcast work on Home does not hurt the core business.

hidden.principle: In an improvement question, find the users who get the most value today and are at risk of leaving; fix what makes them leave before chasing new users.

prompt: How would you improve Tunebox for podcast listeners?

research.text: Daily commuters are 17% of podcast listeners but 64% of podcast listening hours. They follow 5 shows on average.
46% of commuters who stopped listening on Tunebox kept listening to the same shows in another podcast app the next month.
8 of 11 commuters complained that an episode starts from the beginning when they move from phone to car. Several said new episodes of their shows are buried under music on Home.
Music-first listeners are the biggest group, but 65% of them say they are not interested in podcasts.
160 app reviews this quarter asked for transcripts or finer speed control, mostly from people learning a language.
Podcast creators sent 70 requests for audience analytics.

segments.name: Daily commuters
segments.description: Listen to a few shows every day on the way to and from work, across phone and car.

segments.name: Music-first listeners
segments.description: The largest group; tried a podcast once or twice.

segments.name: Language learners
segments.description: Use podcasts to study a language.

problems.statement: No transcripts and only coarse speed control.
Offline downloads fail or fill the phone.
New episodes of followed shows are buried under music on Home.
It is hard to discover new shows worth trying.
Episodes lose their place when switching between phone and car.

solutions.name: New episodes shelf
solutions.description: A shelf at the top of Home with new episodes of followed shows.

solutions.name: Smart downloads
solutions.description: Download the next episode of followed shows on wifi and delete finished ones.

solutions.name: Transcripts and speed
solutions.description: Synced transcripts and speed from 0.5x to 3x.

solutions.name: Resume on any device
solutions.description: Sync the playback position across phone, car and web in real time.

solutions.name: AI show recommendations
solutions.description: Recommend new shows from each person's music taste.

metrics.name: Podcast DAU
metrics.definition: Daily users who play any podcast.

metrics.name: App store rating
metrics.definition: Average rating in the app stores.

metrics.name: Shows followed per user
metrics.definition: Average number of shows a podcast listener follows.

metrics.name: Weekly podcast retention of commuters
metrics.definition: Share of commuters who listen to a podcast on Tunebox in two consecutive weeks.
